subject: DPA + Order Form: dataflow delegation and execution timeline
messages:

Subject: DPA and Order Form: kickoff and ask

Hi Marta —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Per our procurement conversation, I’m attaching the current Order Form (v3) and our standard DPA for your legal team to review. Two quick asks to help us scope the redlines on our side:

- Can you confirm which SCCs you prefer us to adopt (controller-to-processor standard clauses or processor-to-processor)?
- Do you need a separate Transfer Impact Addendum or TIA evidence package for Acme’s EU data flows to US-hosted instances?
- Any mandatory language your procurement team requires in the Order Form around data residency, logging, or incident notification timelines?

If you can send any redlines or a mark-up by EOD Thursday (Jan 14) we’ll prioritize review with legal and product. Looping in Laura from contracts who will track the timeline.

Attachments:
- OrderForm_D-ACME-4721_v3.pdf (Order form draft)
- Redwood_Standard_DPA_v2.docx (internal attachment referenced)

Thanks —

From: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@acmehealth.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jason Lee <jason.lee@acmehealth.com>, procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: 2027-01-12T14:08:00Z
Subject: Re: DPA and Order Form: kickoff and ask

Alex —

Thanks for sending this through. Our legal team did a quick pass and attached a marked-up DPA with comments. Summary of the key asks from Acme:

1) Roles: We need a clearer delegation matrix in the DPA that lists Acme as controller and Redwood as processor, plus explicit subprocessor approval process.
2) SCCs: We prefer Controller-to-Processor SCCs (latest EU commission text). Please confirm Redwood can sign those without qualifying language.
3) Transfer Impact: Acme requires a Transfer Impact Addendum and TIA evidence for any subprocessors or cloud regions outside the EEA — specifically for US-hosted processing.
4) Audit & Logs: We require 90 days of audit log retention evidence and confirmation of support for customer-initiated forensic requests.
5) Order Form: Add a short clause clarifying data residency commitments per product route; we’ve annotated the Order Form where this should sit.

Attachment: Acme_DPA_Redline_v1.docx (track changes + commentary)

We’re running procurement timelines tightly this quarter. Can you get an initial Redwood response to the redline and whether you accept the SCCs request by EOD Jan 14? If not, provide a short list of open items and an estimated date to finalize.

Best,
Marta Ruiz
Head of Legal Operations | Acme Health
marta.ruiz@acmehealth.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-01-13T10:22:00Z
Subject: RE: DPA and Order Form: kickoff and ask

Alex / Laura —

Saw Acme’s redline. Quick internal notes after a first pass:

- SCCs: We can accept Controller-to-Processor SCCs, but need to preserve our standard exceptions around embedded third-party model providers. Recommend: accept SCCs but include a limited carve-out for model vendor subprocessors and provide a named-subprocessor commitment window (30 days notice + option to object).
- Transfer Impact: We should offer TIA summary (high level) and commit to producing evidence (logs, certification details) within 10 business days after countersignature. Full technical evidence may require engagement with infra (ops) — schedule might be 2–3 weeks.
- Audit/log retention: 90 days is reasonable but we’ll flag cost/retention trade-offs; product may push for 30 days by default with paid retention add-on.
- Order Form residency clause: Product needs the exact route names to map to regions; ask Acme which routes they expect to pin to EU-only.

Action items I propose:
1) Draft Redwood_DPA_Response_v1.docx accepting SCCs, proposing the processor-subprocessor delegation matrix, and offering TIA summary + timeline.
2) Alex to confirm which route(s) Acme expects to keep EU-only so product can verify.
3) Laura to prepare a short change-log and negotiation matrix for procurement.

I’ll review the DPA response doc this afternoon and flag any technical blockers.

—Karthik
Director, Legal & Privacy | Redwood Inference
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@acmehealth.com>, procurement@acmehealth.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-01-14T16:45:00Z
Subject: RE: DPA and Order Form: kickoff and ask

Marta —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the helpful annotations. Attached is our initial response (Redwood_DPA_Response_v1.docx) — short summary below and proposed next steps: 

Summary of Redwood position:
- SCCs: We can accept Controller-to-Processor SCCs as requested. No material qualifiers on SCCs themselves; we will append an Attachment listing delegated subprocessors and our model-vendor carve-out language (30-day notification and objection right).
- Transfer Impact Addendum: We will provide a TIA summary and a package of evidence (data flow diagram, subprocessors list, log-retention proof). Estimated delivery: TIA summary within 5 business days after countersign; full evidence package within 15 business days.
- Audit/Logs: We confirm support for customer-initiated forensic requests; default retention we can commit to 30 days included, with an option to purchase 90-day retention as an add-on.
- Order Form: We implemented a short residency clause and annotated where Acme should indicate the route(s) to pin to EU-only.

Next steps:
1) Please review the attached Redwood_DPA_Response_v1.docx and confirm whether the model-vendor carve-out and 30-day default + paid retention add-on are acceptable.
2) If agreed, I’ll send the executable Order Form + DPA via DocuSign for countersignature. DocuSign link: https://app.docusign.com/exec?doc=redwood-acme-dpa-4721
3) Procurement sign-off requested by Jan 21 to meet your quarter close.

Attachments in this message: Redwood_DPA_Response_v1.docx (response with proposed tracked changes and delegation matrix)

Thanks — speak soon,
